events.title: Earliest Human Activity
events.description: Archaeological evidence shows human activity in the Malay Peninsula and Borneo. These early inhabitants are ancestors of modern Malaysian indigenous people (Orang Asli).

events.title: Austronesian Migration
events.description: Austronesian-speaking peoples migrated from Taiwan through the Philippines to the Malay Peninsula and Borneo, bringing agricultural and maritime technology. Malays belong to the Austronesian language family.

events.title: Early Indianized Kingdoms
events.description: Indian culture spread to the Malay Peninsula through trade, forming Indianized kingdoms like Langkasuka and Kedah. Hinduism and Buddhism began spreading, with Sanskrit influencing Malay language.

events.title: Srivijaya Empire Rule
events.description: Sumatra's Srivijaya Empire controlled the Malacca Strait, ruling parts of the Malay Peninsula. Srivijaya was a powerful maritime commercial empire and Buddhist center.

events.title: Malacca Sultanate Founded
events.description: Parameswara (said to be the last prince of Srivijaya) established the Sultanate of Malacca. Malacca rapidly developed into a major trading port due to its strategic location.

events.title: Islam Becomes State Religion
events.description: Sultan Parameswara of Malacca converted to Islam, taking the name 'Iskandar Shah.' Islam became Malacca's state religion and spread throughout the Malay Archipelago through trade.

events.title: Malacca's Golden Age
events.description: Malacca became Southeast Asia's most important trading center, controlling the Malacca Strait. Merchants from China, India, Arabia, and Europe gathered here. Zheng He's voyages frequently visited Malacca.

events.title: Portuguese Conquest of Malacca
events.description: Portuguese General Alfonso de Albuquerque led forces to capture Malacca; the Sultan fled to Johor. Portugal ruled Malacca for 130 years, monopolizing spice trade.

events.title: Johor Sultanate Founded
events.description: Descendants of Malacca Sultans established a new sultanate in Johor, continuing resistance against Portugal. Johor became the most powerful state in southern Malay Peninsula.

events.title: Dutch Occupation of Malacca
events.description: The Dutch East India Company allied with Johor to capture Malacca, ending Portuguese rule. Dutch ruled Malacca for nearly 200 years, but Malacca's commercial importance gradually gave way to Batavia (Jakarta).

events.title: Bugis and Minangkabau Migration
events.description: Bugis people from Sulawesi and Minangkabau from Sumatra migrated in large numbers to the Malay Peninsula, enriching Malaysia's ethnic composition.

events.title: British Occupy Penang
events.description: The British East India Company acquired Penang Island from the Sultan of Kedah, establishing George Town. This was Britain's first foothold in the Malay Peninsula.

events.title: Raffles Establishes Singapore
events.description: British Stamford Raffles established a trading post in Singapore. Singapore quickly replaced Malacca as the region's trading center.

events.title: Anglo-Dutch Treaty
events.description: Britain and the Netherlands signed the Anglo-Dutch Treaty, dividing spheres of influence. North of the Malacca Strait went to Britain, south to the Netherlands. This treaty established boundaries for modern Malaysia, Singapore, and Indonesia.

events.title: Straits Settlements Founded
events.description: Britain merged Penang, Malacca, and Singapore into the Straits Settlements. These three ports became Britain's trade and administrative center in Southeast Asia.

events.title: Pangkor Treaty and British Protectorates
events.description: Britain began intervening in Malay sultanate internal affairs, signing the Pangkor Treaty. Malay states gradually became British protectorates, with British 'Residents' effectively controlling each state.

events.title: Federated Malay States Founded
events.description: Four sultanates—Perak, Selangor, Negeri Sembilan, and Pahang—formed the Federated Malay States under unified British administration. Kuala Lumpur became the capital.

events.title: Mass Chinese and Indian Immigration
events.description: Large numbers of Chinese immigrants came to Malaya for tin mining and trade, Indians for rubber plantations. This formed Malaysia's multiethnic society.

events.title: Bangkok Treaty
events.description: Britain and Siam signed the Bangkok Treaty, with Siam ceding Kelantan, Terengganu, Kedah, and Perlis to Britain. These states became 'Unfederated Malay States.'

events.title: Japanese Invasion of Malaya
events.description: As the Pacific War began, Japanese forces invaded Malaya from Thailand. British forces retreated repeatedly, with Japan occupying all of Malaya and Singapore in just 70 days.

events.title: Japanese Occupation Period
events.description: Japan occupied Malaya and North Borneo for three and a half years. Japanese rule was harsh, with Chinese facing persecution. The Malayan Peoples' Anti-Japanese Army (mainly Communist) conducted guerrilla warfare.

events.title: British Reoccupation
events.description: After Japan's surrender, Britain reoccupied Malaya. But the war had already sparked Malayan nationalism and independence consciousness.

events.title: Malayan Union Proposal
events.description: Britain proposed the Malayan Union, attempting unified administration of Malaya with equal citizenship for Chinese and Indians. But Malays strongly opposed, and the plan failed.

events.title: Federation of Malaya Established
events.description: The Federation of Malaya was established, preserving sultans' status and restricting non-Malay citizenship. Same year, the Malayan Communist Party launched armed rebellion, beginning the 'Malayan Emergency.'

events.title: Malayan Emergency
events.description: The Malayan Communist Party conducted guerrilla warfare in jungles, with British and Malayan government conducting anti-communist operations. The war caused thousands of deaths, with the government ultimately victorious.

events.title: First Federal Election
events.description: Malaya held its first national election, with the Alliance Party (comprising UMNO, MCA, and MIC) winning decisively. Tunku Abdul Rahman became Chief Minister.

events.title: Malayan Independence
events.description: The Federation of Malaya gained independence from Britain, with Tunku Abdul Rahman as first Prime Minister. August 31 became Malaysia's National Day (Independence Day).

events.title: Malaysia Formation
events.description: The Federation of Malaya merged with Singapore, Sabah (North Borneo), and Sarawak to form the Federation of Malaysia. However, Brunei ultimately did not join.

events.title: Indonesia-Malaysia Confrontation
events.description: Indonesia opposed Malaysia's formation, launching military confrontation (Konfrontasi). Indonesian guerrillas infiltrated Borneo and Malay Peninsula, causing border conflicts.

events.title: Singapore Leaves Federation
events.description: Due to political and racial tensions, Singapore was expelled from Malaysia, becoming an independent nation. Malaysia lost its most economically developed state.

events.title: May 13 Incident
events.description: Post-election racial riots erupted between Malays and Chinese, causing hundreds of deaths. The government declared a state of emergency and parliament was suspended. This event profoundly impacted Malaysian politics.

events.title: Tun Razak Becomes PM
events.description: Tun Razak succeeded Tunku Abdul Rahman as second Prime Minister. He promoted 'Rukunegara' (National Principles) and the New Economic Policy, attempting to foster ethnic harmony and Malay economic position.

events.title: New Economic Policy
events.description: The government implemented the New Economic Policy (NEP), aiming to eradicate poverty and correct economic imbalances. The policy gave Malays (Bumiputera) economic privileges, sparking controversy but continuing today.

events.title: Mahathir Becomes PM
events.description: Mahathir Mohamad became the fourth Prime Minister, beginning a 22-year rule (1981-2003). He promoted industrialization and modernization, making Malaysia a newly industrialized country.

events.title: Proton Car Production Begins
events.description: Malaysia's national car Proton began production. This was a flagship project of Mahathir's industrialization policy, symbolizing Malaysia's technological progress.

events.title: Vision 2020
events.description: Mahathir proposed 'Vision 2020,' aiming to make Malaysia a developed nation by 2020. This vision drove Malaysia's rapid development.

events.title: Multimedia Super Corridor
events.description: The government launched the Multimedia Super Corridor (MSC) project, establishing a high-tech corridor between Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya to promote IT industry development.

events.title: Asian Financial Crisis
events.description: The Asian Financial Crisis severely impacted Malaysia's economy, with the ringgit plummeting. Mahathir refused IMF assistance, implementing capital controls and fixed exchange rate policies, with the economy gradually recovering.

events.title: Anwar Arrested and Reformasi Movement
events.description: Deputy PM Anwar Ibrahim was arrested due to political disagreement with Mahathir, charged with sodomy and corruption. Supporters launched the 'Reformasi' democracy movement demanding reforms.

events.title: Putrajaya Becomes Administrative Capital
events.description: Newly built Putrajaya replaced Kuala Lumpur as the federal government administrative center. Putrajaya was part of Mahathir's modernization plan.

events.title: Abdullah Badawi Becomes PM
events.description: Mahathir retired, with Abdullah Badawi becoming fifth Prime Minister. He proposed 'Islam Hadhari' (Islamic Civilization) concept, implementing more moderate policies.

events.title: BN Loses Two-Thirds Majority
events.description: Opposition coalition achieved breakthrough in elections, with BN losing two-thirds parliamentary majority and five state governments for the first time. This marked a major change in Malaysia's political landscape.

events.title: Najib Becomes PM
events.description: Najib Razak became sixth Prime Minister. He promoted '1Malaysia' concept and economic transformation plan, but his tenure saw the 1MDB scandal erupt.

events.title: 1MDB Scandal
events.description: The 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) founded by Najib erupted in massive corruption scandal, with billions of dollars missing. This became one of the world's largest financial scandals, damaging Malaysia's international image.

events.title: Historic Change of Government
events.description: 92-year-old Mahathir led Pakatan Harapan to defeat Barisan Nasional in elections, achieving Malaysia's first change of government since independence. Mahathir became PM again; Najib was prosecuted for corruption.

events.title: Sheraton Move
events.description: Pakatan Harapan internal split triggered political crisis. Mahathir resigned, with Muhyiddin becoming PM without elections, forming Perikatan Nasional government.

events.title: COVID-19 and Political Turmoil
events.description: Malaysia implemented Movement Control Order to combat COVID-19, with the economy damaged. Meanwhile, political turmoil continued, with Muhyiddin's government facing confidence crisis.

events.title: Ismail Sabri Becomes PM
events.description: Muhyiddin resigned after losing parliamentary majority support, with Ismail Sabri becoming ninth Prime Minister. Malaysia experienced three PMs in 17 months, with continued political instability.

events.title: Hung Parliament Election
events.description: Election results produced hung parliament, with no coalition gaining majority seats. After days of negotiation and King's intervention, Anwar finally formed unity government.

events.title: Anwar Becomes PM
events.description: Anwar Ibrahim was sworn in as the tenth Prime Minister, realizing his 25-year dream of becoming PM. Anwar promised to fight corruption, promote reforms, and unite the nation.

events.title: Najib Imprisoned
events.description: Former PM Najib was sentenced for 1MDB corruption, with Federal Court rejecting appeal. Najib began serving 12-year sentence, marking a milestone in Malaysia's anti-corruption history.
